summary.text: Alexander Lopez is the One Nation candidate for Footscray at the 2026 Victorian election. Born in Argentina, he came to Australia with his family in 1975 and they made their home in Melbourne's west. He is a financial controller whose working life of over three decades spans transport, logistics, property and manufacturing, and he once worked as an accountant for Papua New Guinea's electricity commission.

sources.title: Footscray: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Ana Flores is the Family First candidate for Footscray at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Her party page says she was born in Cuba, came to Australia with her family as a child in 1972, and has worked as a general practitioner for about 40 years. She says her medical career shaped her concerns about late-term abortion and about gender ideology being taught to primary school children, and she wants parents to have a bigger say in decisions about their children.

priorities.text: More support and information for women facing hard decisions about a pregnancy
Parents' right to be involved in medical and other decisions about their children
Opposing the teaching of gender ideology as settled fact in primary schools

summary.text: Catherine Cumming is standing as an independent for Footscray at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. A Catherine Cumming served on Maribyrnong City Council from 1998 to 2018, including two terms as mayor, then sat in the Legislative Council for Western Metropolitan Region from 2018 to 2022, elected for Derryn Hinch's Justice Party but sitting as an independent. The ABC's seat history notes that independent Catherine Cumming contested Footscray at each state election from 2002 to 2014; no source we read explicitly ties the 2026 nomination to her, though the name, seat and label all match.

summary.text: Elena Pereyra is the Greens candidate for Footscray at the 2026 Victorian election, her second run for the seat after she finished runner-up to Labor in 2022. She won a place on Maribyrnong City Council for Wattle Ward in 2024. Trained as an architect, she is working on a doctorate about housing held in common and is a board member of Cohousing Australia.

occupation.text: Councillor and PhD candidate; formerly an architect

previous_candidacies.election: 2018 Victorian state (Legislative Council, fourth on the Greens ticket)

priorities.text: Our local area deserves a representative who will listen to them.
Affordable housing and living, and development built around the community
Walking and cycling, urban ecology and action on climate
Green neighbourhoods and a strong local arts and culture scene

summary.text: Hai Dinh is standing as an independent for Footscray at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. On his campaign website he says he has lived in the Footscray area for many years and studied a Bachelor of Technology in computer technology at Victoria University. His campaign, run under the banner Renew Footscray, focuses on safety, local jobs and business, and community services, and has taken up local planning disputes such as the future of the former Footscray Hospital site.

priorities.text: I want stronger action on crime and antisocial behaviour
Help for local businesses, more investment and livelier shopping strips
Better community facilities and essential services, with residents given a real say
Open decision-making and careful use of public money
Keeping 3.5 hectares of the old Footscray Hospital land as public open space

summary.text: Jasmine Duff is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Footscray at the 2026 Victorian election. She describes herself as a community organiser, lighting technician and union member, and spent several years working for the NSW State Emergency Service. She ran for the party in the federal seat of Fraser in 2025.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Victorian Socialists candidate of this name; no source links that race to the Footscray candidate.

Many more public homes and more funding for housing organisations, instead of selling off public housing
Free public transport and free childcare
Lifting welfare payments above the poverty line
More hospitals, schools, parks and transport for Melbourne's growing west

summary.text: Jess Marsh is running for Footscray as an independent at the 2026 Victorian election, with the endorsement of the Voices of the Inner West group. A human rights lawyer, she has worked for government, for the United Nations and at the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre in Footscray, and she is now senior legal counsel at the Sunrise Project Australia. She grew up in Hong Kong and has made Yarraville her home for over a decade.

prior_roles.role: Senior legal counsel and assistant company secretary

priorities.text: Cleaner air in the west, including filters on the West Gate Tunnel stacks and fewer trucks on local streets
A pause on approving data centres in residential areas until their health and environmental effects are independently assessed
Planning decisions made with real input from residents
More and better public schools nearby, and protected green spaces
Stronger integrity and oversight in government

summary.text: Katie Hall has been the Labor member for Footscray in the Legislative Assembly since 2018, when she succeeded the retiring Marsha Thomson. She was re-elected in 2022 and has served as a parliamentary secretary in several areas, among them creative industries and homes. She is recontesting Footscray in 2026.

summary.text: Tim Chang is the Liberal candidate for Footscray at the 2026 Victorian election. A dentist, he and his wife opened a practice in Yarraville almost twenty years ago, and the business now has sites across the inner west. He campaigned with local residents and traders over the level crossing removal at Anderson Street in Yarraville.

priorities.text: Safer streets, lower costs and better services, in line with the Liberal campaign
Local concerns about the Anderson Street level crossing removal
